# Model card: GL coding suggestion

| | |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Suggest a GL account and cost centre for an invoice line that the organisation's coding history cannot code. |
| Workflow | pay |
| Code | `pairly_pay.coding.model_suggestion` |
| Prompt | `pay_coding_suggest` version `v1`, file SHA-256 `a388591ab4189b03...` |
| Output schema | `ModelCoding` |
| Model tiers, cheapest first | `small` (anthropic `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, openai `gpt-6-luna`) then `large` (anthropic `claude-sonnet-5-5`, openai `gpt-6.1-sol`) |
| Temperature | 0.0 |
| Output token limit | 512 |
| Confidence threshold to accept | none |

## Inputs

The line description and the codes in force. Nothing else.

## Outputs

`ModelCoding`: codes that must exist in the lists in force, or the answer is dropped.

## Human oversight

A suggestion only. History-based suggestions come first; the model one is never applied by itself, whatever the settings. A person confirms the codes, and corrections feed later suggestions.

## Limits

* Knows only the description, not the organisation's habits.
* Asked on request from the coding screen.
* Every call is logged in `model_calls` (prompt version and hash, model, inputs, output, tokens, cost) and fails closed: no model means a person does the step.

Structural checks only (`python -m evals.structural`), on the committed recordings: scripted answers, not model output. They say whether every recorded output fits the schema, holds no banned content or em dash, passes the component's own deterministic check and points only at its input. They are not quality judgments: how good a draft is needs a live model and people.
